conflicts.description: The lamp matrix table on printed page 1-33 (repeated on PDF page 117, and on 2-34 where the scan fills in column 8's pin digit) prints columns on J138-1 to J138-7 and J138-9 and rows on J133-1, J133-2 and J133-4 to J133-9, while the lamp matrix schematic on printed page 2-34 draws columns on J137-1 to J137-8 and rows on J133-1 to J133-8; the 1-33 lamp-circuit example also routes its column through J137. Read address by address at native resolution, both sheets give the same eight column and row wire colours and the same addresses 11-88, and the schematic names no lamps. Matrix address/name identity is preserved from the printed matrix table; neither connector reading is synthesized into wiring fields. Resolution path: a photograph of an unrestored machine's power driver board lamp connectors, showing whether the column harness plugs J137 or J138 and which J133 pins the rows use.
conflicts.rationale: A wiring-detail disagreement, not a conflict (runbook, What is not a conflict): the two sheets differ only in connector labels and agree on every lamp's address and on its column and row wires, so nothing a recreation consumes is in doubt. Lamp identity follows the printed matrix table, and each lamp note states both connector readings.

PinMAME's generic end-of-stroke bit for this flipper. Terminator 2's flippers are cabinet-wired (FLIP_SWNO(12,11) with no FLIP_SOL), so core.c's EOS simulation never runs and nothing synthesizes it; no CPU-side contact is wired to it, so it rests open (0) unless a host writes it. On this pre-WPC-95 generation wpc_r serves the flipper column at WPC_FLIPPERS (0x3FD4). No Williams T2 program ROM in the authorized library addresses that register, but the FreeWPC 0.19 build (t2_f19) reads it, so the bit stays optional rather than unused.

mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough and outhole

mechanisms.behavior: The retained saucer stack uses switch 78, a 0-degree/50-strength kick, and kick-force variance 3.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and auto plunger

mechanisms.behavior: The retained left lock stack uses switch 51 and kicks at 160 degrees with strength 13.
mechanisms.label: Left lock saucer

mechanisms.behavior: The retained top lock stack uses switch 55, kicks at 270 degrees with strength 5, and has kick-force variance 6.
mechanisms.label: Top lock saucer

mechanisms.behavior: cvpmMech one-solenoid/reverse/non-linear; solenoid 11, length 240, steps 240; home switch 33 window 0-5, mark switch 32 window 98-105; visual callback uses CurrentPos=aNewPos/3. The retained script moves T2_Gun and its held ball, not a keyframed or magnet cannon.
mechanisms.label: Motorized cannon traverse

mechanisms.behavior: Solenoid 2 fires the loaded ball from switch 31 by -CurrentPos at strength 45, clears the loaded ball, and is commanded by the grip trigger switch 34.
mechanisms.label: Cannon fire and gun-loaded kicker

mechanisms.behavior: SolSkull is the retained callback: manual solenoid 1 Ball Popper opens the skull/ball path from switch 76. The callback name is retained and is not turned into a virtual skull device.
mechanisms.label: Skull ball popper

mechanisms.behavior: One A-14615 drop target under the skull, sensed by switch 77. Solenoid 28 (AE-26-1200 reset coil) raises it; the retained script models this as dtDrop1.SolDropUp. Solenoid 12 (the A-14908 knock-down sub-assembly's SM1-26-600 coil, 2-23 parts list) drops it from below without a ball strike; neither retained table fires it in play (the VPW script has no callback for 12), but the ROM's solenoid test pulses it, so a recreation that fits it must drop the target and close switch 77 on a pulse.
mechanisms.label: Single skull drop target with knock-down

mechanisms.behavior: SolAPlunger fires Plunger1, the left outer-lane kicker saver; it is distinct from the auto-plunger output 9.
mechanisms.label: Left outer-lane kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Two C-13174 lower flipper assemblies with FL-11630 coils, powered from the power driver board (right Blu-Yel J109-7, left Gry-Yel J109-5) through the Game-On relay (31) and switched by the cabinet buttons; there is no CPU flipper drive. PinMAME fabricates public 45-48 from the buttons for animation, and the matrix copies 11/12 tell the ROM a button is held.
mechanisms.label: Direct-wired lower flippers

Manual physical device: Knock Down; printed on the 1-28 and 2-38 solenoid tables, the 2-39 Solenoid Locations list and the 3-8 interboard wiring table. The drop-target knock-down coil. The 2-23 A-14615 1-Bank Drop Target Assembly parts list includes item 23, A-14908 Target Knock Down Assembly (01-8647-L actuator, A-14913 frame and eyelet, SM1-26-600 coil), bolted beside the AE-26-1200 reset coil of solenoid 28; the 1-28 solenoid table and the 2-39 Solenoid Locations list print solenoid 12 as Knock Down with that SM1-26-600 coil, and the 2-39 drawing prints balloon 12 on the drop-target assembly. The 2-38 copy of the solenoid table prints the row as Not Used and blanks its part-number cell, but keeps its Low Power type, Brn-Yel wire, J127-5 connection and Q52 transistor, and the 3-8 interboard table wires Solenoid 12 Brown/Yellow to J127-5 and Q52. The L-8 ROM's T.4 SOLENOID TEST names solenoid 12 KNOCK DOWN with the printed BRN-YEL wire and pulses public 12. The retained VPW script has no SolCallback(12), and the nFozzy comparison script keeps a SolDTdown handler for it commented out as a cut feature. The coil is fitted and wired, and the ROM's test drives it; neither retained table fires it in play, which is how Not Used on 2-38 reads. A recreation fits the coil so that a pulse drops the target and closes switch 77. The knock-down sub-assembly is bolted to the A-14615 drop-target assembly; the placement is the drop target the coil acts on, and the 2-39 drawing prints balloon 12 on that assembly.
